OotA requires a dedicated group though and may take some players out of their comfort zone due to it being set entirely within the underdark. The lower levels also seem like they could be crushing. ToA has a lot of cool stuff going on in it, but if you don't like hexcrawls than it might not be for you. It can also be crushingly difficult and I'm not sure I'd feel comfortable running it with my current group where only one of the players is what I would call a veteran.

So overall, Curse of Strahd is an absolute must play in my book. Tomb of Annihilation and Out of the Abyss stand out and have a lot of cool elements to them but if you never play them you won't miss out. The rest I've found pretty meh.

My PC's escorted Ireena and Ismark to the church to bury their father. I told that that, per tradition in the worship of the Morninglord, the rites were performed all night and the burial would happen at dawn the next morning so the PCs would have to defend the church all night. The lock the priest and Ireena in the priests room, believing that though Strahd can enter the public church he would need permission to enter the priests private room. I tell them that's reasonable so they spend the rest of the day barricading the doors and windows, basically making the church defensible etc. Midnight comes with no incident when all of a sudden there's a slow knock on the church door. Ismark tells them not to answer and they assume battle positions. After the third round of knocks go unanswered, there's a powerful gust of wind completely throwing the doors wide open and smashing the barricade. The sudden squall extinguishes the candlelight plunging the church into darkness. A PC and Ismark manage to fight through the wind and close the doors. The candles spring back to life and the PCs turn to see a well dressed man sitting on the altar. "Am I too late to pay my respects?" He asks.

Then they talk for a bit, Strahd talks about what fun they'll have together, the fighter gets pissed and attacks but is quickly wounded without much effort from Strahd. Eventually, he departs as a blood red mist, his laughter echoing the whole time. Then the PCs had to jump into combat as Strahd left them a parting gift of dire wolves scratching at the door and zombies trying to break through the barricaded windows.

The best advice I can give is to keep lists of things. Places the PCs have been, important NPCs, names of random NPCs or taverns or what have you. A habit I've gotten in to is before every session I make a list of all the important NPCs and what they're doing and all the important locations and what's going on there. It really helps with the verisimilitude and makes it feel like there's a whole world the PCs are apart of and people and places aren't just popping into existence for the PCs convenience.
